title: “Be still and know” in chaos — Psalms 46
paragraphs: “Be still and know” in chaos — Psalms 46

Chaos is loud.
God is not.
“Be still, and know that I am God.” — Psalm 46:10
That verse was never written for a peaceful beach with soft music in the background.
It was spoken into war, shaking nations, roaring waters, trembling mountains. Psalm 46 is not a calm chapter. It is a crisis chapter. The earth gives way. Kingdoms totter. Everything feels unstable.

And right there—
not after the storm,
not when the panic is over,
not when the bills are paid and the tears stop—
God says:
Be still.

Not because the chaos is fake.
Not because your fear is foolish.
But because He is still God in the middle of it.

Here’s what we miss:
“Be still” does not only mean relax. It carries the sense of stop striving, release your grip, surrender the illusion of control. In other words:
Stop acting like your panic can do what only God can do.

Brother, sister—
the storm around you may be real,
but it is not reigning.
God is.
Psalm 46 does not promise a life without trouble. It promises the presence of God within trouble:

“God is our refuge and strength,
a very present help in trouble.”
— Psalm 46:1

Very present.
Not distant.
Not late.
Not confused.
Not overwhelmed.
And that points us straight to Jesus.

Because the greatest chaos was never just around us. It was inside us—sin, fear, guilt, rebellion, unrest. But Christ stepped into our storm. He lived the righteousness we could not live, died the death we deserved, and rose again to give peace that the world cannot manufacture.

So when Psalm 46 says, “Be still and know,” it is not a call to empty your mind.
It is a call to anchor your soul in the God revealed fully in Jesus Christ.

Be still.
He is Savior.
He is Lord.
He has not lost the room.

Today, breathe deep and surrender what you cannot carry.
The chaos may still be screaming.
But Christ is still King.

Prayer:
Lord, when my heart is noisy and my world feels like it is breaking apart, teach me to be still before You. Quiet my striving. Break my unbelief. Help me know—not just say—that You are God. Anchor me in Jesus, my refuge, my peace, and my hope. Amen.
